working_title: Evaluating Component-Level Executability and Recovery Barriers in Archived Python Research Code from Ecology and Hydrology
study_design: Exploratory multiple-case study using purposively selected archived repositories
research_aim: To examine the executability of selected archived scientific Python components, document observed execution barriers and recovery interventions, and evaluate limitations in interpreting archive age and execution outcomes.

research_questions.RQ1: To what extent can selected components of archived Python research code in ecology and hydrology be executed in a contemporary computing environment?
research_questions.RQ2: What dependency, compatibility, configuration and source-code barriers are observed, and which documented interventions enable limited recovery?
research_questions.RQ3: What methodological limitations arise when interpreting archive age and execution outcomes across heterogeneous repositories?

operational_distinctions.code_availability: Archived source code can be accessed.
operational_distinctions.component_executability: A selected original function, test, cell or script executes under documented conditions.
operational_distinctions.workflow_executability: The complete intended computational workflow executes under documented conditions.
operational_distinctions.result_reproduction: Reported scientific outputs are independently regenerated and compared against the relevant publication or authoritative reference.

potential_contributions: A scope-sensitive classification of execution outcomes.
A documented taxonomy of observed execution barriers.
Case-level evidence of limited recovery interventions.
An explicit distinction between component execution and scientific result reproduction.
An assessment of why heterogeneous baseline tests limit archive-age comparisons.
publication_claims_not_supported: All 15 full workflows were successfully executed.
Published results were reproduced for all candidates.
A statistically reliable archive-age relationship has been established.
Missing dependencies prove temporal code decay.
Human recovery effort was measured in minutes.
The purposive sample represents all ecology and hydrology research software.
